I ran one search. It turned up several GitHub issues about hydration mismatches that browser extensions appear to cause, though none is a single canonical fix.

- **Extensions are a known trigger.** The error text React prints says that it can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded. That same message appears quoted across several issues.
- **Issue #25924 (React 18.2, 2022):** A reporter traced a mismatch to a script tag that the React DevTools extension injected after the body tag, and asked whether the `suppressHydrationWarning` escape hatch should be applied to it. The issue is still marked unconfirmed.
- **Issue #31895 (closed as not planned):** A reporter found the same kind of error with a video speed controller extension, using a Next.js canary build with a React 19 release candidate.
- **Discussion #72035 (Next.js, React 19):** The ColorZilla extension added a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute to the page. Disabling the extension fixed it, and one commenter shared a workaround that removes the attribute before hydration and uses a MutationObserver to stop it returning.
- **Issue #33133 (React 19.1.0, closed as not planned):** This one is not about extensions. Combining `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with `suppressHydrationWarning` reportedly clears the server-rendered DOM during hydration. Issue #32975 describes a related change in React 19.
- **Issue #36169 (React 19.2.4, open):** A `<script defer>` inside `<head>` reportedly triggers hydration errors, and the reporter says the docs should state that it is discouraged.

If you're debugging a specific case, the first thing to check is whether the mismatch goes away in a clean browser profile with extensions disabled.

content.text:
Yes. There isn't one canonical React 19 issue for this, but these are the closest matches. I only read search-result titles and snippets, not the issue threads, so check each one's status yourself.

- **[facebook/react#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924)** is "Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React dev tools) may cause hydration errors". It's the most direct match on extensions causing hydration errors. It was filed against React 18, but it's the one people cite.
- **[react/react#31895](https://github.com/react/react/issues/31895)** is a hydration error with the Video Speed Controller Chrome extension on React 19 RC (via Next.js 15 canary). That makes it the React 19-specific one.
- **[vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035)** covers the ColorZilla extension injecting a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute, which causes the error with Next.js 15 and React 19. It's a Next.js discussion rather than a React issue, and it includes workarounds.
- **[facebook/react#24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430)** reports a hydration mismatch from plugins injecting a script tag at the top of the document. It's an older, related report.

**Common workaround:** Add `suppressHydrationWarning` to `<html>` or `<body>`, where extensions typically inject attributes. You can also test in a clean browser profile to confirm an extension is the cause.

Sources:
- [Issue #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924)
- [Issue #31895](https://github.com/react/react/issues/31895)
- [Next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035)
- [Issue #24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430)
